channel.title: Books on Pods
channel.description: Conversations about books and plays, old and new. Two hosts read the best passages and discuss their impressions as well as what critics and scholars have said about them.
channel.itunes:summary: Conversations about books and plays, old and new. Two hosts read the best passages and discuss their impressions as well as what critics and scholars have said about them.
channel.itunes:author: BooksonPods

item.title: Love's Labour's Lost 1. The Oath and the Arrival
item.description: Act 1 Scene 1 and Act 2. The academy oath, Berowne's resistance, the Princess's arrival, and the first battle of wits.

item.title: Love's Labour's Lost 2. Below Stairs
item.description: Act 1 Scene 2 and Act 3. Armado, Moth, Costard and Jaquenetta, the remuneration joke, and Berowne's 'And I, forsooth, in love!'

item.title: Love's Labour's Lost 3. Letters Gone Astray
item.description: Act 4 Scenes 1 and 2. The Princess's hunt, Armado's letter read aloud, Holofernes and Nathaniel, and Berowne's sonnet on its way to the king.

item.title: Love's Labour's Lost 9. The Whole Play
item.description: The whole play, ending included: from Theobald, Johnson and Hazlitt's dismissals to Pater, Carroll and Bloom, the feminist and historical readings, the School of Night, Love's Labour's Won, the stage history, and why the play still matters.

item.title: Julius Caesar. The Full Play
item.description: The complete play, read in full (about 2 hours 25 minutes).

item.title: Julius Caesar 8. The Whole Play
item.description: The whole play in one long conversation: Brutus and Caesar, the funeral speeches, the crowd, the politics from Welles to Central Park, Booth and Lincoln, Nyerere's Juliasi Kaizari, Portia and the Roman ideal, and why the play keeps being acted over in states unborn.

item.title: Julius Caesar Extra. Two Old Romans
item.description: The hosts play an old Brutus and an old Antony, thirty years after a Philippi where nobody died, arguing over honour, rhetoric, the easy choice, and what the critics have said about them both.

item.title: Parable of the Sower. Octavia E. Butler
item.description: Octavia Butler's 1993 novel, set in a burning 2024 California: prophecy or warning, Earthseed and hyperempathy, Butler's life and notebooks, the critics, the opera, the Mars landing site, and how prescient it really is. No spoilers for the ending.

item.title: The Correspondent. Virginia Evans, and the Life in Letters
item.description: A lifelong letter writer tries to convert a co-host who has written about five: the pen-pal life, the epistolary novel from Ovid and Richardson to Laclos, Austen, Bellow and The Color Purple, and Virginia Evans's sleeper hit The Correspondent. No spoilers.

item.title: Julius Caesar 1. The Feast of Lupercal
item.description: Act 1 Scenes 1 and 2. The cobbler and the tribunes, the Lupercal, the Soothsayer, Cassius as Brutus's mirror, the Colossus speech, Caesar's deaf ear, Casca's crown report and 'Greek to me', with Rymer, Kahn, Foakes, Vawter, Miles, Anson, MacCallum, Liebler, Girard and Hazlitt.

item.title: Julius Caesar 2. Storm and Conscience
item.description: Act 1 Scene 3 and Act 2 Scene 1. The night of omens, Cicero's warning about construing signs, Brutus's orchard soliloquy and the forged letter, the conspirators' meeting, Portia's wound and Ligarius, with Fortin, Charney, Miles, Vawter, Theobald, Montaigne, Liebler, Kahn, Hazlitt and Anson.

item.title: Julius Caesar 3. The Ides
item.description: Act 2 Scene 2 to Act 3 Scene 1. Calpurnia's dream and Decius's reading of it, Artemidorus, the northern star, the assassination and Et tu Brute, the bloodied hands, How many ages hence, and Antony alone with the body, with Plutarch, Suetonius, Girard, Paster, Kahn, Charney, Phillips, MacCallum, Knight and Hazlitt.

item.title: Julius Caesar 4. Two Speeches
item.description: Act 3 Scene 2. Brutus's prose oration and Antony's 'Friends, Romans, countrymen', the will, the mantle and the wounds, Mischief, thou art afoot, with Wills on rhetoric and chiasmus, Plutarch on Brutus's laconic style, Appian, Suetonius, Paster, Charney and Baldwin on Elizabethan schooling.

item.title: Julius Caesar 5. Mob and Death List
item.description: Act 3 Scene 3 and Act 4 Scene 1. Cinna the poet torn for his name, Antony, Octavius and Lepidus pricking names, with Plutarch on Helvius Cinna, Welles's 1937 staging, the 2017 Public Theater production, Girard, Jack Cade, Ulrici, MacCallum, Foakes and Wills, and the death of Cicero.

item.title: Julius Caesar 6. The Quarrel
item.description: Act 4 Scenes 2 and 3. Brutus and Cassius in the tent at Sardis, the bribes and the friendship, the intruding poet, Portia's death reported twice, the tide in the affairs of men, Lucius's song and Caesar's ghost, with Johnson, Digges, Dryden, Theobald, Platter, Plutarch, Cicero on friendship via Wills, Miles, Kahn, Vawter, Phillips, Fortin and Hazlitt.

item.title: Julius Caesar 7. Philippi
item.description: Act 5. The parley of words before blows, Cassius's birthday and his turn from Epicurus, the misread battle and Titinius's wreath, O Julius Caesar thou art mighty yet, Brutus's farewell, and Antony's eulogy, with Plutarch, Horace's lost shield, Theobald, MacCallum, Wills, Charney, Phillips, Dowden and Girard.

item.title: The Infinite Sadness of Small Appliances. Glenn Dixon, and Why We Cede Control
item.description: A robot vacuum named Scout, a grieving widower, and the Grid. Why humans hand over control, with the Roomba photo leak, the Arkansas care algorithm, ElliQ, Kant, the Grand Inquisitor, Fromm, Tim Wu, Langdon Winner, Bainbridge, Carr, Zuboff, Forster's The Machine Stops, Postman, Whitehead and Ruth Schwartz Cowan. Then why there are no phones, with Mark Weiser, Albert Borgmann, Turkle, Bradbury and Haidt. No spoilers.

item.title: The Devotion of Suspect X. Drishyam, August 2, and the Tenth of March
item.description: With a guest, a Malayalam film critic who finally read Keigo Higashino's novel. Drishyam and Mohanlal, the 2014 denial and the legal notice, the case that Drishyam is built on the novel, spoilers included, from the public phone calls and the ticket stubs in the programme to the date trick and the substitute body, why the denial was a mistake, whether Drishyam 2 is original, the Chinese remake that outearned every official adaptation, and why we root for Georgekutty, with Hobbes, Locke, Partha Chatterjee, Walter Benjamin, Hitchcock, Antigone and Derrida.

item.title: Responsive Math Teaching 1. The Story Being Sold
item.description: What Sold a Story Season 2 argues about Zig Engelmann, Direct Instruction and Project Follow Through, set against the 1960s, the New Math and the War on Poverty. The Follow Through evaluation and the House and Glass critique No Simple Answer, the 2018 Direct Instruction meta-analysis, the maths wars, and an introduction to Mary Kennedy's five persistent problems of teaching as the lens for the series.
